'''William Edgar Fulton''' (born August 29, 1939) is an American [[mathematician]], specializing in [[algebraic geometry]].

==Education and career==
He received his undergraduate degree from [[Brown University]] in 1961 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate]] from [[Princeton University]] in 1966. His Ph.D. thesis, written under the supervision of [[Gerard Washnitzer]], was on ''The fundamental group of an algebraic curve''.<ref name="MathGen">{{MathGenealogy|id=10281}}</ref>

Fulton worked at Princeton and [[Brandeis University]] from 1965 until 1970, when he began teaching at Brown. In 1987, he moved to the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="sp1996">[http://www.ams.org/notices/199611/comm-steele.pdf Announcement of the] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110206074044/http://www.ams.org/notices/199611/comm-steele.pdf |date=2011-02-06 }} 1996 [[Steele Prize]]s at the [[American Mathematical Society]] web site, accessed July 15, 2009.</ref> He moved to the [[University of Michigan]] in 1998, retiring in 2020.<ref>[https://lsa.umich.edu/content/dam/math-assets/math-document/W--Fulton-memoir.pdf University of Michigan retirement memoir] accessed April 17, 2026.</ref> As of 2026, Fulton had supervised the doctoral work of 24 students at Brown, Chicago, and Michigan.<ref name="MathGen" />

Fulton is known as the author or coauthor of a number of popular texts, including ''Algebraic Curves'' and ''Representation Theory''.

==Awards and honors==
In 1996, he received the [[Steele Prize]] for mathematical exposition for his text ''Intersection Theory''.<ref name="sp1996" />  Fulton is a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] since 1997; a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] from 1998, and was elected a foreign member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite news |title=View from the Chair's Office - Fulton Named Distinguished Oscar Zariski University Professor |url=https://studylib.net/doc/14946457/view-from-the-chair-s-office---fulton-named-distinguished... |access-date=3 April 2022 |publisher=University of Michigan}}</ref> In 2010, he was awarded the [[Steele Prize]] for Lifetime Achievement.<ref name="ams2010">[http://www.ams.org/ams/press/steele-lifetime-2010.html AMS Newsroom] AMS announcement of 2010 Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2012-12-29.</ref>
